skip_rationale: Not a skip -- real discovery pass for a genuine new visual direction (user explicitly asked for 'más cyberpunk' onboarding), done after two prior turns of improvising tokens from memory instead of reading real sources (user caught both). Project: NexaBank-Mobile (/home/danidev/Documentos/Dev/NexaBank/NexaBank-Mobile), scope: Splash + Phone screens only (user explicitly excluded OTP/Register/Pin from this pass).

referent.take: Layered glow technique (stacked box-shadow/text-shadow at increasing blur radius, RN equivalent: textShadowColor/Offset/Radius for text, stacked semi-transparent Views for shapes). Motion: spring-based entrances (stiffness~120/damping~20 feel), fade+translateY(16px->0) over ~540ms ease-out with ~120ms stagger between elements, hover/press = scale(1.03) + shadow lift over 200ms. Scanline/grid-line as a SUBTLE atmosphere layer, not a dominant motif. Typography principle: 'glows but doesn't shout -- signage seen through condensation', i.e. soft diffuse glow, not sharp/loud. 2026 fintech-specific finding: a SINGLE calibrated neon accent (not multi-color) that pulses/breathes (lights up on event, fades back to muted dark) at 10-15% surface coverage max -- this is the restraint principle that keeps it 'neo-fintech premium' rather than full HUD.
referent.leave: Orbitron display font (breaks the already-committed Geist brand font). Multi-neon palette (cyan/magenta/purple from the Neon Noir reference) -- user chose 'neo-fintech premium con acentos cyberpunk' over 'cyberpunk denso/HUD', so NexaBank's existing single-lime-accent identity stays the only neon color, not a rainbow. Dense/constant glitch effects, CRT-scanline-as-dominant-texture, angular clip-path panel shapes, hexagonal grid overlays, holographic wireframe iconography -- all explicitly 'cyberpunk denso' territory the user did not pick.

style.name: Obsidiana y Lima + neon-noir accents (restrained, single-accent glow/motion layer on top of the existing brand, not a style replacement)
